topic: How Can a Rogue Wave Rise Out of Nowhere?
script:
Imagine an ocean wave towering above the waves around it. Sailors call it a rogue wave, and it can strike without much warning.

Most ocean waves are formed by wind. They travel at different speeds and in different directions, creating a constantly changing surface.

Sometimes several waves overlap at just the right moment. Their crests add together, building one unusually tall wave before separating again.

Ocean currents can also concentrate wave energy. When waves move against a strong current, they may become steeper and more dangerous.

Rogue waves are real, but they are not magic walls of water. Scientists study wave measurements and ocean conditions to understand when these rare giants may form.
